headline: Organic growth fades, margins compress, outlook held
summary_short: Bruker's Q1 FY2026 revenue of $823.4M rose 2.7% y/y (down 4.4% organically) as GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.02 from $0.11 on new preferred-stock dividends and non-GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.31 from $0.47; the company reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of $3.57-3.60B revenue and $2.10-2.15 non-GAAP EPS.
summary_long: Q1-26 revenue of $823.4M rose 2.7% y/y as a 4.5% FX tailwind and 2.6% M&A contribution masked a 4.4% organic decline, led by a 5.0% organic drop in the core Bruker Scientific Instruments segment amid soft US academic demand and tariff headwinds. GAAP operating income fell to $10.2M from $31.8M and GAAP diluted EPS to $0.02 from $0.11; non-GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.31 from $0.47 as restructuring, acquisition, and impairment charges widened the GAAP-to-non-GAAP gap. Cash fell to $133.4M from $298.8M q/q after a $181.3M debt repayment; free cash flow was $47.0M. BSI bookings grew high-single-digits organically, book-to-bill above 1.0x for a third straight quarter. Bruker reaffirmed FY2026 guidance unchanged: $3.57-3.60B revenue, $2.10-2.15 non-GAAP EPS.

drivers.explanation: Reported revenue grew on a 4.5% FX tailwind and 2.6% M&A contribution; organic revenue fell 4.4% on soft US academic demand and tariff headwinds pressuring the core Scientific Instruments segment.

GAAP operating income fell as the release's own reconciliation excludes $74.0M of restructuring, acquisition, intangible-amortization, and impairment charges to reach non-GAAP operating income of $84.2M, down from $101.7M a year earlier.

Net income attributable to Bruker fell as the same restructuring, acquisition-related, and impairment charges reducing operating income also reduced pre-tax income, per the release's own non-GAAP reconciliation table.
GAAP diluted EPS fell further than net income because $10.9M of new Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock dividends (none a year earlier) were deducted before the per-share calculation.
Operating cash flow rose y/y as higher depreciation and amortization ($58.3M vs $50.4M) more than offset a larger inventory build (-$47.2M vs -$28.4M) in the reconciliation to net income.
Cash fell q/q and y/y as Bruker repaid $181.3M of long-term debt and paid $11.0M in preferred and $7.6M in common dividends this quarter, per the financing-activities section.
Long-term debt declined as Bruker repaid $181.3M of debt this quarter with no new debt issuance, per the cash-flow statement's financing-activities section.

CEO cited soft US academic demand, tariff impacts, and FX headwinds pressuring results, though performance came in ahead of internal expectations; FY2026 guidance was reaffirmed unchanged and Q2 organic growth is expected to resume.
